references.text: The same chapter describes that both the priest and the one who burns the heifer must wash their clothes and remain unclean until evening, following the same pattern as for the one who gathers the ashes.
The verse confirms that this is to be a permanent statute, using the same expression found in verse 10.
A permanent statute applying to both Israelites and foreigners living among them, reflecting the same principle of including foreigners.
Describes uncleanness until evening and washing of clothes, following the same cleansing pattern.
The same law shall apply to the native-born and to the foreigner living among you, illustrating the principle that foreigners are included in the laws.
A permanent statute for all generations: one law shall apply to you and to the foreigner living among you.
The same rule applies to the foreigner as to the native-born, affirming equality before the law.
Hebrews refers to the ashes of the heifer that cleanse the unclean for external purity, pointing to Christ's blood as a greater cleansing.
